probe: M022 T002 — document.elementFromPoint over the tool's closed, pointer-events: none host

method.page: about:blank, in a tab the control script opens and closes: the probe builds the page element and the host it measures, so the reading does not depend on a server, a fixture or a build
method.host: the probe creates the host the product will create — id angular-ai-devtools-host, position: fixed, attachShadow({ mode: 'closed' }), pointer-events: none, appended to document.documentElement (SYNTHESIS decision 5) — and one page element under it, at one known point
method.point: the centre of a 200 x 80 px fixed box at viewport point (140, 80), the same point on every profile
readings: baseline — document.elementFromPoint before the host exists, proving the point is over the page element and the measurement is not vacuous
measured — the product configuration: the host with pointer-events: none
comparison — the same probe host with pointer-events: auto, for comparison only; never the product configuration
method.identity: the answer is classified by node reference as the tool's host (node probe-host, or probe-host-inner-node when an inner node of the closed root is returned unretargeted), a page element, nothing, or other
method.cleanup: the probe removes the host and the page element in a finally block and re-counts document.querySelectorAll('[id^="angular-ai-devtools"]'); every row reports toolElementsAfter 0, so nothing was left in the page and no page global was written
method.version: the page's user agent is reduced to <major>.0.0.0, so the build that answered was read over one CDP session with Browser.getVersion (a read)

ruling.statement: The hover path maps a hit that returns the tool's own host — or any node inside its closed root — to "the tool, not a candidate", and never to a picked element, while a hit that returns a page element is used as the candidate. The mapping is correct whether or not an engine retargets an inner node of a closed root to its host, so the picker does not lean on the 2026 CSSWG retargeting resolution or on any engine's behaviour: the four measured readings return the page element, and the comparison reading, which does return the host, is recorded to show how a hit-testable host answers, never to be depended on.
ruling.pointerEvents: the host's product value is pointer-events: none on every profile and inside its closed root, so the host cannot swallow a pick; a value that made the host hit-testable would turn every hover over the drawn rect into the tool instead of the element beneath it

visualViewport.statement: `visualViewport.scale` is read for nothing: pinch zoom moves no layout coordinate, so no rect input depends on it and pinch zoom is out of scope (INTENT § Scope, Out). `visualViewport.width`/`height`/`offsetLeft`/`offsetTop` are read only to clamp the label inside the viewport.

doesNotSettle.question: what does elementFromPoint answer over the product's live overlay on an inspected Angular page, rather than over a probe-built host on about:blank?
doesNotSettle.settledFor: the shape the overlay will build — closed root, pointer-events: none, appended to documentElement — measured on all four charter profiles; the answer there is the page element on every profile.
doesNotSettle.stillOpen: the probe host carries no rect, label or per-frame style writes, and the measured page is about:blank; a page element that is itself pointer-events: none, a transformed ancestor or a nested shadow root of the page was not measured.
doesNotSettle.probeThatWouldSettleIt: run the same three readings inside the armed picker on the counter fixture once T008 draws a rect: hover a page element under the drawn rect and record what the hover path resolves.

doesNotSettle.question: do engines other than these four retarget a closed root's inner node to its host?
doesNotSettle.settledFor: Chrome 156, Chrome 158, Edge 156 and Edge 158 — the four charter profiles — each return the host in the comparison reading, so retargeting is observable there.
doesNotSettle.stillOpen: Firefox and Safari ship no Prompt API and sit outside the charter, so neither was driven; the comparison reading is evidence about these four builds, not a platform guarantee.
doesNotSettle.probeThatWouldSettleIt: re-run spikes/probes/hit-test.js on any added profile before claiming the mapping holds there.

verdict: measured: on all four charter profiles a point over a closed, pointer-events: none host returns the page element beneath it, and the same host with pointer-events: auto returns the host — so the picker maps a host hit to the tool and a page-element hit to the candidate, never leaning on retargeting
